about: P57 T4 library judge: top300 by usage + sample100, 3x3 grids, score 1-10 per cell (recognisable, silhouette, Toy Box style, broken mesh). Odd sheets Codex, even sheets Opus, every tenth both (agreement). score = mean of the judges that read the cell; null = unread after two attempts.
question: The attached image is a contact sheet of 9 numbered 3D game models (cells 1 to 9, row by row; each cell shows one model from a 3/4 view, its number in the top-left corner and its size in metres at the bottom). Our game has a "Toy Box" look: chunky, tactile, toy-like low-poly models with clean readable silhouettes and bright solid colours – not glassy, techy, photo-scanned or noisy. Score every cell from 1 to 10 as a model a player would see in a finished mobile game, judging four things: recognisable = a player can tell at a glance which single object it is; silhouette = a clean, readable shape; style = fits the Toy Box look; broken = torn mesh, holes through it, loose fragments, a melted blob or an empty cell. Anchors: 1-3 broken or not recognisable; 4-5 recognisable but blobby, scan-like, noisy or off-style; 6-7 a decent game asset with visible flaws; 8-9 a polished toy-like model from a finished game; 10 flawless. Reply only with the JSON the schema asks for: one entry per cell with cell (its number), name (what you think it is, 1-3 words), score (whole number 1-10), recognisable, broken, styleFit (true when it fits the Toy Box look) and reason (at most 15 words: the main flaw or strength).
